text:
chandra: Heads-up — scaling training jobs on eu-west4-prod hitting scheduling failures. Pods fail with IP allocation errors and GPU nodepools are saturating. Seen during a 6x A100 rollout.

chandra: error snippet:
```
Warning  FailedCreatePodSandBox  30s  kubelet, gke-eu-west4  failed to allocate pod IP: no available addresses
E0901 12:03:21.123456  1234 pod_workers.go:191] Error syncing pod ... failed to "CreatePodSandbox": rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to setup network for sandbox: failed to allocate ip: range exhausted
```

mike: Sounds like secondary IP range exhaustion on the nodepool subnet or mask too small. Which nodepool and what's the pod secondary range size?

chandra: Nodepool is `training-a100-eu-west4` created with default /24 secondary range for pods. We also bumped `--max-pods-per-node` to 110 to fit more pods on GPUs but that just increases IP demand. GPU quota also at 0 available for A100 in eu-west4.

sam: Can you paste the quick checks you ran? gcloud outputs for quotas and subnets?

chandra: Quick checks:
```bash
gcloud compute regions describe europe-west4 --project=redwood-prod --format='json(quotas)' | jq '.quotas[] | select(.metric=="GPUS")'
# shows limit 8, usage 8 -> 0 available

gcloud compute networks subnets describe redwood-prod-pods-eu4 --region europe-west4 --format='value(secondaryIpRanges)'
# shows pods-range size 10.132.16.0/24 (256 IPs)
```

lena: If we increase GPU quota and expand pod ranges, what's the expected monthly delta for 8 more A100s vs using cross-region fallback? Need rough $ for finance sign-off. :thinking:

chandra: Rough on-demand: ~€18k/month for 8 x A100s (training nodes running 24/7). If we use spot/short-lived training, significantly lower. Cross-region stopgap (eu-west1) adds egress and latency but might be cheaper short-term.

mike: Short-term workarounds:
- create a new nodepool in eu-west1 where A100 quota exists and use nodeSelector/affinity for training jobs
- create a new pod-secondary-range (bigger mask /20) and migrate nodepool to use it
- split training cluster from inference to avoid IP fragmentation

Command to add a bigger secondary range and new nodepool (example):
```bash
# reserve a new secondary range
gcloud compute networks subnets update redwood-prod-pods-eu4 \
  --region=europe-west4 \
  --add-secondary-ranges=pods-range-2=10.132.0.0/20
# create nodepool using the new secondary range
gcloud container node-pools create training-a100-eu4-2 \
  --cluster=eu4-prod-cluster --region=europe-west4 \
  --node-taints=training=true:NoSchedule \
  --accelerator=type=nvidia-a100-v4,count=1 \
  --node-labels=workload=training \
  --enable-ip-alias --cluster-secondary-range-name=pods-range-2
```

infra-bot: Created internal ticket INFRA-842 (https://redwood.internal/INFRA-842) to track: GPU quota request + secondary range expansion + stopgap nodepool.

gcp-support-bot: Support case created with GCP: case 123456789. GCP engineer requested justification and expected sustained usage, ETA 48-72 hours. Link: https://console.cloud.google.com/support/cases/123456789

sam: I'll add the justification: training CI + nightly hyperparam sweeps + scheduled model retrain. I'll also loop in finance for spend approval.

oliver: Another option: reduce per-node max pods and spread pods across more nodes (trade CPU for IPs), or use vertical packing of training processes per GPU. Also consider using node-local-subnet allocation to reduce fragmentation.

mike: Agree. For immediate relief I'll spin up a eu-west1 nodepool and migrate two queued jobs there. chandra — can you tag the jobs that are flexible?

chandra: Tagged flexible jobs with `training.flexible=true`. Moving queued ones now.

lena: Approving provisional spend for up to €20k/month for temporary A100 usage while we wait on quotas — will formalize after finance review. :white_check_mark:

sam: Action items: 1) I will reply to GCP case with justification (today). 2) Mike will create eu-west1 nodepool as stopgap (in 15m). 3) Chandra will mark flexible jobs and monitor. 4) Infra-842 will track full follow-up (secondary range resize + permanent capacity plan).

chandra: Thanks — I'll post cluster scheduling metrics and follow up in INFRA-842. :partyparrot:
